Fraud Detection Platform Architecture

The MFS Fraud Detection platform is a real-time ML-powered system that scores every incoming transaction for fraud probability within 50ms SLA.

System Components

  • Feature Extraction Service: Consumes raw transactions from Kafka topic mfs.txn.raw, computes real-time features (velocity, merchant risk, device fingerprint, geolocation anomaly), and publishes enriched events to mfs.txn.features. Runs on mfs-fraud-pod-01 under svc-fraud-engine service account.
  • Fraud Scoring Engine: XGBoost model (v2, ONNX format) served via gRPC. Deployed across mfs-fraud-pod-01 and mfs-fraud-pod-02 in mfs-prod OpenShift namespace for high availability.
  • Model Registry: MLflow-based model versioning with A/B testing support. Metadata stored in mfs_fraud_db.model_registry on pghost-prod-02.mfs.internal.

Data Flow

Transaction Ingestion → Feature Extraction → Fraud Scoring → Decision (approve/review/decline) → Alert Generation

Related Work Items

FRD-100 (Feature), FRD-101 (Model Pipeline), FRD-102 (Feature Extraction), FRD-103 (Model Versioning)

Real-time Transaction Monitoring System Design

The transaction monitoring system provides continuous surveillance of financial transactions using velocity-based rules and statistical anomaly detection.

Velocity Monitoring

Tracks transaction rates across three dimensions:

  • Per-account: Flags accounts exceeding normal transaction frequency
  • Per-merchant: Identifies merchants with unusual inbound transaction patterns
  • Per-device: Detects device-based fraud rings

Time windows: 1 minute, 5 minutes, 1 hour, 24 hours. Thresholds configurable via YAML rules with hot-reload (no service restart required).

Anomaly Detection

Two-stage approach: Z-score analysis for univariate anomalies, isolation forest for multivariate pattern detection. Severity levels: HIGH (>0.9), MEDIUM (0.7-0.9), LOW (<0.7).

Kafka Topics

Input: mfs.txn.enriched | Output: mfs.alerts.txn

Infrastructure

Deployed on mfs-txn-mon-pod-01 under svc-txn-monitor. Alert data persisted to mfs_fraud_db.alerts table. Consumer group: mfs-txn-monitor-cg.

Related

EPC-202 (Epic), FRD-200 (Feature), FRD-201 (Velocity), FRD-202 (Anomaly), INC0080202 (Kafka lag issue)

Fraud Model Training Pipeline

End-to-end ML pipeline for training, evaluating, and deploying fraud detection models.

Pipeline Stages

  1. Data Extraction: Pull labeled transaction data from mfs_fraud_db.fraud_transactions on pghost-prod-02.mfs.internal. Uses 6-month sliding window.
  2. Feature Engineering: Compute 47 features including velocity aggregates, merchant category embeddings, device fingerprint hashes, and geolocation risk scores.
  3. Model Training: XGBoost with Optuna hyperparameter optimization. Target: AUC-ROC > 0.96, false positive rate < 2%.
  4. Model Evaluation: Held-out test set evaluation plus shadow mode comparison against production model.
  5. Model Export: ONNX format for cross-platform serving compatibility.
  6. Registry: Model metadata, metrics, and artifacts stored in MLflow. Version tracked in mfs_fraud_db.model_registry.

A/B Testing

New models deployed with configurable traffic split (e.g., 90/10 production/candidate). Automated rollback if candidate model false positive rate exceeds production baseline by >0.5%.

Related

FRD-101 (Story), FRD-111 (Model Training Task), FRD-103 (A/B Testing), MR !601

Incident Runbook: Fraud Engine False Positive Spikes

This runbook covers diagnosis and remediation when the fraud scoring engine false positive rate exceeds the 2% SLA threshold.

Detection

Datadog monitor 'Fraud False Positive Rate' fires when FP rate > 2% over 5-minute window. Alert routed to #fraud-oncall Slack channel and PagerDuty.

Immediate Triage

  1. Check Grafana dashboard 'Fraud Engine SLOs' for score distribution shift
  2. Verify feature extraction freshness on mfs-fraud-pod-01: kubectl exec -n mfs-prod mfs-fraud-pod-01 -- curl localhost:8080/health/features
  3. Check model version in production: kubectl exec -n mfs-prod mfs-fraud-pod-01 -- curl localhost:8080/model/version
  4. Review mfs_fraud_db reference table timestamps for staleness

Common Root Causes

CauseIndicatorFix
Stale feature reference datamerchant_risk table last_updated > 24h agoRun feature refresh job; see INC0080201
Model/feature version mismatchModel trained on feature set v(N) but serving v(N-1)Align feature pipeline version with model training config
Training data driftScore distribution diverges from training baselineRetrain model with recent data; trigger FRD-111 pipeline

Rollback

If false positive rate does not recover within 30 minutes: roll back to previous model version via svc-fraud-engine config: kubectl set env deployment/fraud-engine -n mfs-prod MODEL_VERSION=v1

Post-Incident

File ServiceNow incident. Update this runbook. Review in weekly fraud ops meeting.

KYC Document Verification - Architecture Guide

The KYC Document Verification system provides automated identity verification for Meridian Financial Services customers through document authentication, liveness detection, and sanctions screening.

OCR Pipeline

Document text extraction uses Tesseract OCR (v5.3) deployed as a sidecar container on mfs-kyc-pod-01. Supports passports, driver's licenses, and national ID cards. Pre-processing includes deskew, contrast normalization, and noise reduction. Extracted fields (name, DOB, document number, expiry) are validated against issuing authority formats. Confidence threshold: 0.85 minimum for auto-accept; below triggers manual review queue.

Liveness Detection

Anti-spoofing verification powered by AWS Rekognition CompareFaces and DetectFaces APIs. Three-step liveness check: (1) passive liveness from selfie image analysis, (2) active challenge requiring head turn or blink, (3) document-to-selfie face match with similarity threshold > 95%. Results stored in mfs_customers_db.liveness_results on pghost-prod-03.mfs.internal.

Sanctions Screening

Real-time screening against OFAC SDN, PEP lists, and consolidated international sanctions databases. Fuzzy name matching with Jaro-Winkler similarity (threshold 0.88). Screening results persisted to mfs_customers_db.sanctions_hits. Positive matches trigger automatic case escalation to Compliance team.

Document Authenticity Scoring

Multi-factor document authenticity score (0-100) based on: MRZ checksum validation, hologram pattern detection (where supported), font consistency analysis, microprint verification, and metadata EXIF analysis for photo manipulation detection. Score > 80: auto-approved. Score 50-80: manual review. Score < 50: auto-rejected.

KYC Verification Workflow

  1. Customer uploads identity document via mobile app or web portal
  2. Document image quality check (blur, glare, crop detection)
  3. OCR extraction and field validation
  4. Document authenticity scoring
  5. Selfie capture and liveness detection
  6. Face match: document photo vs. selfie
  7. Sanctions and PEP screening
  8. Final verification decision: APPROVED / MANUAL_REVIEW / REJECTED

ML Model Governance & Lifecycle Management

This document defines the governance framework for managing fraud detection ML models throughout their lifecycle at Meridian Financial Services.

Model Versioning Policy

All models follow semantic versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). MAJOR: architecture change or retraining on fundamentally different feature set. MINOR: hyperparameter tuning or incremental retraining. PATCH: bug fixes or configuration adjustments. Every model version must be registered in the MLflow tracking server at mlflow.mfs.internal with full training artifacts, metrics, and lineage metadata. Model registry persisted in mfs_fraud_db.model_registry on pghost-prod-02.mfs.internal.

A/B Testing Requirements

All new model versions must pass A/B testing before full production deployment:

  • Minimum test duration: 7 days
  • Minimum traffic allocation to challenger: 10%
  • Statistical significance threshold: p < 0.05
  • Metrics tracked per variant: AUC-ROC, false positive rate, false negative rate, p99 latency, score distribution
  • Automated rollback trigger: challenger FP rate exceeds champion by > 0.5%

Performance Baselines

MetricThresholdAction if Breached
False Positive Rate< 2%Automatic alert + model review
Detection Rate (True Positive)> 95%Mandatory retraining within 48 hours
AUC-ROC> 0.96Model flagged for investigation
Scoring Latency (p99)< 50msInfrastructure scaling review

Retraining Triggers

  1. Scheduled: Monthly retraining on rolling 6-month data window
  2. Performance drift: KS statistic > 0.05 between training and production score distributions
  3. Data drift: Feature distribution shift detected by Evidently AI monitoring
  4. Incident-driven: Post-incident review recommends retraining
  5. Regulatory: New fraud pattern types identified by compliance team

Approval Workflow for Production Deployment

  1. Data Scientist submits model version with training report
  2. Peer review by ML Engineering team (minimum 2 reviewers)
  3. A/B test results review and sign-off
  4. Model Risk Management (MRM) compliance review
  5. Production deployment approval by ML Engineering Lead
  6. Post-deployment monitoring for 72-hour burn-in period

Champion/Challenger Framework

Production always runs a designated champion model. Challenger models are deployed in shadow mode or with limited traffic split. Promotion criteria: challenger must outperform champion on all baseline metrics for minimum 7 consecutive days. Demotion: automatic if any baseline metric breached for > 1 hour.

Rollback Procedures

  1. Identify target rollback version from model registry
  2. Verify rollback version compatibility with current feature pipeline
  3. Execute rollback: kubectl set env deployment/fraud-engine -n mfs-prod MODEL_VERSION=<target_version>
  4. Verify scoring health check: curl mfs-fraud-pod-01:8080/health/model
  5. Monitor FP rate and latency for 30 minutes post-rollback
  6. File post-rollback incident report

Related

FRD-103 (A/B Testing Story), FRD-111 (Model Training Pipeline), FRD-112 (Model Governance Policy)

Fraud Detection - Operations Runbook

Comprehensive operations runbook for the Meridian Financial Services Fraud Detection platform. Covers incident response, diagnostic procedures, and recovery steps for all fraud detection subsystems.

P1 Incident Scenarios

ScenarioDetectionImpactSLA
Model scoring latency > 50ms p99Datadog monitor 'Fraud Scoring Latency'Transaction approval delays, customer frictionAcknowledge: 5 min, Resolve: 30 min
False positive rate > 2%Datadog monitor 'Fraud FP Rate'Legitimate transactions blocked, revenue lossAcknowledge: 5 min, Resolve: 1 hr
AML engine downtimeDatadog monitor 'AML Engine Health'Regulatory compliance gap, potential finesAcknowledge: 5 min, Resolve: 15 min
Kafka consumer lag > 10,000Datadog monitor 'Fraud Kafka Lag'Delayed fraud detection, increased exposure windowAcknowledge: 10 min, Resolve: 30 min

On-Call Rotation

Primary on-call rotation: Fraud Engineering team (weekly rotation, Monday 09:00 UTC handoff). PagerDuty schedule: fraud-oncall-primary. Slack channel: #fraud-oncall.

Escalation Path

  1. L1 - On-Call Engineer: Initial triage and diagnosis (0-15 min)
  2. L2 - Nadia Kowalski (Fraud Engineering Lead): Escalate if not resolved in 15 min or if root cause unclear
  3. L3 - Sarah Chen (Senior Director, Engineering): Escalate if customer impact confirmed or regulatory risk identified
  4. L4 - VP Engineering: Escalate for P1 incidents exceeding 1 hour resolution time or cross-team coordination required

kubectl get pods -n mfs-prod -l app=fraud-engine

kubectl logs -n mfs-prod mfs-fraud-pod-01 --tail=100

kubectl exec -n mfs-prod mfs-fraud-pod-01 -- curl -s localhost:8080/health

Kibana Queries

Fraud scoring errors (last 1h): kubernetes.namespace:"mfs-prod" AND kubernetes.pod_name:"mfs-fraud-pod-*" AND level:"ERROR"

AML engine exceptions: kubernetes.namespace:"mfs-prod" AND kubernetes.pod_name:"mfs-aml-pod-*" AND level:"ERROR"

Model version changes: kubernetes.namespace:"mfs-prod" AND message:"model version changed"

Pod Restart Procedures

  1. Verify pod state: kubectl describe pod -n mfs-prod <pod-name>
  2. Capture diagnostic logs before restart: kubectl logs -n mfs-prod <pod-name> > /tmp/pre-restart-<pod-name>.log
  3. Rolling restart (preferred): kubectl rollout restart deployment/fraud-engine -n mfs-prod
  4. Single pod restart (if needed): kubectl delete pod -n mfs-prod <pod-name>
  5. Verify pod returns to Ready state: kubectl get pods -n mfs-prod -l app=fraud-engine -w
  6. Validate health check: kubectl exec -n mfs-prod <new-pod-name> -- curl -s localhost:8080/health

Model Rollback Steps

  1. Identify target rollback version: kubectl exec -n mfs-prod mfs-fraud-pod-01 -- curl -s localhost:8080/model/versions
  2. Set rollback version: kubectl set env deployment/fraud-engine -n mfs-prod MODEL_VERSION=<target_version>
  3. Monitor rollout: kubectl rollout status deployment/fraud-engine -n mfs-prod
  4. Verify new model version active: kubectl exec -n mfs-prod mfs-fraud-pod-01 -- curl -s localhost:8080/model/version
  5. Monitor FP rate for 30 minutes post-rollback on Grafana Fraud Engine SLOs dashboard

Kafka Consumer Reset

  1. Stop consumer pods: kubectl scale deployment/txn-monitor -n mfs-prod --replicas=0
  2. Reset offset to latest: kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka-prod.mfs.internal:9092 --group mfs-txn-monitor-cg --reset-offsets --to-latest --execute --topic mfs.txn.enriched
  3. Restart consumer pods: kubectl scale deployment/txn-monitor -n mfs-prod --replicas=2
  4. Verify consumer lag: kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka-prod.mfs.internal:9092 --describe --group mfs-txn-monitor-cg
